system_description.narrative_summary: Across this news window a single dynamic dominates: rising global bond yields and market volatility are forcing central banks and treasuries into reactive posture, testing policymakers' credibility. The system is open — continuous flows of data (inflation, GDP), market prices (yields, FX), policy signals (rate votes, comments, interventions) and institutional responses create reinforcing and balancing feedbacks that propagate stress across asset classes and borders. Short-term policy choices (holds, dissents, interventions) feed market expectations, which in turn alter financing costs and political pressure, creating a self-amplifying loop with international spillovers.
system_description.scope: Monetary policy decisions (Fed, BOJ, ECB, BoE), sovereign bond markets and yield curves (US Treasuries, global long-end), equity market reactions, FX moves (notably USD/JPY), Treasury/sovereign interventions, macro datapoints (inflation, GDP) and market participants (investors, analysts, traders).

variables.name: Short-term policy interest rate
variables.description: The prevailing short-term policy interest rate that anchors immediate borrowing costs across money markets.

variables.name: Long-term bond yield
variables.description: The market-implied yield on long-duration government fixed-income instruments, reflecting long-run return requirements.

variables.name: Yield-curve slope
variables.description: The difference between long-term and short-term yields, capturing term premia and expectations about future policy and growth.

variables.name: Bond market volatility
variables.description: The magnitude and frequency of price and yield fluctuations in fixed-income markets over a given horizon.

variables.name: Inflation rate
variables.description: The rate of change in the general price level over a specified period measured for the economy as a whole.

variables.name: Inflation expectations
variables.description: The aggregated expected future inflation rate as signaled by markets, surveys, and forward-looking indicators.

variables.name: Economic growth rate
variables.description: The pace of change in real aggregate output (GDP) over a defined period, capturing demand-side momentum.

variables.name: Fiscal financing pressure
variables.description: The degree of pressure on public-sector borrowing needs and rollover requirements relative to available funding sources.

variables.name: Bond market liquidity
variables.description: The depth and ease with which fixed-income positions can be transacted without causing large price movements.

variables.name: Credit spread level
variables.description: The average premium over risk-free yields demanded by investors to compensate for credit and default risk across issuers.

variables.name: Exchange rate level
variables.description: The nominal level of a currency in bilateral or effective terms relative to other currencies.

variables.name: FX intervention risk
variables.description: The market-implied likelihood and pressure for official intervention in foreign-exchange markets to influence currency values.

variables.name: Policy communication tone
variables.description: The tone, clarity, and frequency of public communications and forward guidance issued by monetary policy actors.

variables.name: Central-bank credibility
variables.description: The level of market and public confidence in the central bank's ability and commitment to deliver its stated price-stability mandate.

variables.name: Market rate expectations
variables.description: The market-implied expected path of short-term policy rates over upcoming policy horizons as signaled by tradable instruments.

variables.name: Cross-asset correlation
variables.description: The degree to which returns across major asset classes move together, indicating potential channels for contagion.

catalysts.title: Pressure on Fed to raise rates
catalysts.description: Bond-market repricing and internal Fed dissents increase pressure on the Fed to tighten policy or signal greater hawkishness.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Bond market is calling Warsh’s bluff', 'Three Fed Officials Say Inflation Should Have Prompted Higher Rates'.

catalysts.title: Continued rise in long-term Treasury yields
catalysts.description: Momentum in the long end keeps pushing benchmark yields higher, sustaining pressure on borrowing costs and fiscal roll‑overs.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: '30-Year Yield at 19-Year High', 'U.S. Treasury Yields Rise', 'Long bond takes fright'.

catalysts.title: US Treasury potential/ongoing USD/JPY intervention
catalysts.description: US Treasury warnings and reported interventions create a high near-term chance of coordinated or follow‑on FX support operations in USD/JPY.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Treasury Warns Banks It Might Intervene', 'US Treasury intervenes to support yen', 'Dollar slips against yen'.

catalysts.title: BOJ stance and further yen intervention risk
catalysts.description: BOJ's hawkish warnings on inflation and recent yen operations raise the chance of policy shifts or additional intervention that affect global rates and FX.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'BOJ holds rates at 1%, warns of core inflation exceeding 2%', 'Yen surges, analysts suspect intervention'.

catalysts.title: ECB pressure to hike after rising eurozone inflation
catalysts.description: Stronger-than-expected eurozone inflation increases the odds the ECB signals or enacts tighter policy in upcoming meetings.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Eurozone inflation rises to 2.9%', 'Rates Outlook: ECB Ready to Hike'.

catalysts.title: Big Tech earnings test market sentiment
catalysts.description: Earnings from major tech firms could rekindle risk-off swings, altering stock-bond correlations and short-term demand for safe assets.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Magnificent 7 results set to test broadening US stock market', 'From a Fed decision to Big Tech earnings...volatile market'.

catalysts.title: Japan quake disrupts supply chains
catalysts.description: Quake-related stoppages at auto and chip plants may produce supply disruptions that feed through to growth and price pressures.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Japan quake halts auto and chip plants, testing supply chain resilience'.
